Both parts of the report are addressed.

## Root cause of the retry failure

`Files.Add` passes the raw `io.Reader` (an `os.File`) straight into `Raw.Do`. `http.NewRequest` only sets `req.GetBody` for in-memory types (`bytes.Buffer/Reader`, `strings.Reader`); an `os.File` gets a `Body` but **no `GetBody`**. The retry transport (`pipedrive/retry.go:86`) uses `GetBody != nil` to decide whether a request body can be replayed (`canReplayBody`), so 429/5xx retries were skipped entirely. Call-log recordings work because `multipartbody.NewFile` returns a `*bytes.Reader` (GetBody set).

## Changes

**`pipedrive/raw.go`** — `Raw.Do` now calls `makeBodyReplayable(req)` after building the request. Non-replayable bodies are buffered into memory once and served from a fresh reader on each retry (a seeker can't be reused because the HTTP transport closes the request body after each attempt).

**`internal/multipartbody/multipartbody.go`** — added `NewFileWithFields` (writes extra form fields alongside the file part, sorted for determinism); `NewFile` now delegates to it.

**`pipedrive/v1/files.go`** — added `Files.Upload(ctx, fileName, content io.Reader, opts ...AddFileOption)` that builds the multipart body for you (matching the call-log recording ergonomics) with optional association options `WithFileDealID/PersonID/OrganizationID/ProductID/ActivityID/ProjectID/LeadID`, `WithAddFileQuery`, and `WithAddFileRequestOptions`. `Add` is unchanged.

**Tests** — `TestRawClient_Do_RetriesSeekableFileBodyOn429`, `TestRawClient_Do_RetriesNonSeekableBodyByBuffering`, `TestFilesService_Add_RetriesOnRateLimitWithFileBody` (end-to-end `Files.Add` with a real temp file), and `TestFilesService_Upload` / `TestFilesService_Upload_RequiresNameAndContent`.

## Testing performed
- `go test ./...` — all pass
- `go test -race` on new tests — pass
- `gofmt -l` — clean
- `go vet ./pipedrive/...` — clean

## Breaking changes / migration notes
- None: `Add`, `AddRemoteFile`, `LinkRemoteFile`, and `Update` are unchanged.
- Behavior note: any `io.Reader` body sent through `Raw.Do` that is not already in-memory is now buffered into memory (previously streamed). This is required to make retries safe and matches the existing call-log recording behavior. Files already passed as `*bytes.Reader`/`*strings.Reader` are unaffected.
- Recommended usage for the report's use case: `client.Files.Upload(ctx, "doc.pdf", f, WithFileDealID(dealID))` retries correctly on 429 out of the box; `client.Files.Add` also now retries.
